An authority submission visual decides whether a project clears approval. A hero image decides whether an off-plan buyer signs and whether the finance clears. A catalogue of product visuals decides whether a furniture brand launches on time. Practices, developers and brands know this. What they struggle with is production capacity. The work is lumpy, in-house 3D talent is hard to hire and harder to keep, and freelance marketplaces make consistency difficult to hold from one job to the next. Rendify solves that with a subscription partner model and a production pipeline that sits at the front of this industry. AI accelerates our modelling, materials, lighting and iteration. Experienced 3D specialists art direct every scene and review every frame before it reaches a client. That is the whole argument, and it is a strong one: AI-enhanced production, human reviewed. You get AI speed with human results, and you will be selling that distinction to buyers who care a great deal about what actually lands in their inbox. The role, plainly Full sales cycle. You find it, you qualify it, you demo it, you propose it, you negotiate it, you close it, and then you keep the account and grow it. Work the inbound. Around 80% of your pipeline comes from warm leads Rendify generates and hands to you. You start with live pipeline in your first week and spend your time selling. Build the rest yourself. review_candidates.title: Bernie's Book Bank - Executive Director, Chicagoland Chapter
review_candidates.description: Organizational Overview: Bernie’s Book Bank Better futures begin with books. Bernie's Book Bank is a mission-driven organization dedicated to ensuring that every child has access to books and the opportunity to build a home library of their own. Founded in Lake Bluff, Illinois in 2009, Bernie's Book Bank has delivered more than 32 million free, high-quality books to children through a growing network of schools, early childhood programs, hospitals, clinics, and community partners. Each child receives eight free books a year, matched to their reading level, hand-delivered, every year from birth through sixth grade, to keep. The organization is focused on a simple but consequential idea: children who have books of their own are better positioned to develop the literacy skills they need to succeed. Bernie's Book Bank prioritizes children and communities with the greatest need, including Title I schools and low-income communities where children may otherwise have limited access to books. Recent independent research has further validated the impact of this approach. In April 2026, a five-year randomized controlled trial of the program was published in PNAS stating that children who received books every year gained roughly half to two thirds of an additional year of reading growth, reinforcing the organization's belief that book ownership is a meaningful and scalable intervention. Today, Bernie's Book Bank operates through a national chapter model, with Chicago serving as its flagship and most mature market. The organization also has chapters in Milwaukee and the Florida Suncoast, with an ambitious vision for continued national growth. The Chicagoland Chapter serves roughly 315,000 children a year across a six-county service area, and will hand-deliver approximately 2.5 million books to them in 2026. Across all three chapters, the plan for 2026 is to deliver roughly 3 million books to approximately 375,000 children, putting millions of books directly into the hands of those who need them most. Bernie's Book Bank is entering an important new chapter. With a strong operating model, a compelling body of evidence, deep community relationships, and an ambitious goal of reaching one million children nationally by 2029, the organization is building the infrastructure and leadership capacity needed to grow its impact. This includes strengthening its national systems while ensuring that the Chicago chapter remains a strong, well-supported, and appropriately resourced foundation for that growth. Position Summary: Executive Director, Chicagoland Chapter The Executive Director, Chicagoland Chapter, joins Bernie's Book Bank at an important moment in the organization's evolution. Reporting directly to the Chief Executive Officer, the Executive Director will serve as the senior leader of the organization's flagship chapter and will have primary responsibility for its financial sustainability, fundraising, operations, external relationships, and continued growth. This is a highly external-facing, development-forward leadership opportunity. The Executive Director will inherit a base of philanthropic, corporate, and community relationships, while also having the opportunity to build a more sophisticated and diversified development operation. The successful candidate will be a visible leader in the Chicagoland community, personally cultivating relationships with high-capacity individuals, corporate leaders, foundations, and community partners. Additionally, the Executive Director will serve internally as the chief operator, leading across functions and overseeing the Chicagoland Chapter's approximately $5 million budget. The Executive Director will manage organizational priorities, support a talented team, and ensure that revenue growth translates into programmatic growth. This is an opportunity for a leader who is energized by growth, comfortable with change, and excited by the opportunity to take a well-performing chapter to its next level of success and mission impact. Above all, the Executive Director will help ensure that Chicago remains a powerful engine for Bernie's Book Bank while serving as a strong advocate for the chapter as the organization continues to build its national footprint. Key responsibilities include: Partner with the CEO and national leadership on enterprise growth, contributing to the development of a national infrastructure while helping ensure that the lessons, relationships, and practices developed in Chicago inform the organization's broader growth. Provide strong operational leadership, partnering with the Senior Operations Manager and broader operations team to ensure that fundraising and program growth translate into efficient and effective book processing, volunteer engagement, distribution, and community impact. Lead the Chicagoland Chapter's fundraising and revenue strategy, establishing annual and multi-year goals and personally driving major individual, corporate, foundation, and partnership opportunities. Build and manage a significant portfolio of donors and prospects, cultivating high-capacity individuals, corporate leaders, foundations, and community partners and personally soliciting and stewarding major commitments. Partner with the Founder on the transition of long-standing donor relationships into a managed Chicagoland portfolio, treated as a deliberate program with named relationships and timelines rather than a one-time handoff. Diversify and strengthen the chapter's revenue model, developing new opportunities across major gifts, corporate partnerships, sponsorships, foundations, events, and volunteer-to-donor engagement. Build a high-performing development function, assessing the current structure, identifying gaps, recruiting key talent, and establishing the systems, roles, goals, and accountability needed to support sustained growth. Serve as the senior external leader for Chicago, representing Bernie's Book Bank with donors, corporate and civic leaders, philanthropic institutions, community organizations, media, and other key stakeholders across Chicagoland. Lead and engage the Chicagoland Board, partnering with the Board to strengthen its transition from an advisory body to a governing board and activating members as ambassadors, donors, connectors, event participants, and fundraisers. Lead chapter financial stewardship, overseeing budgeting, forecasting, revenue performance, and financial decision-making in partnership with national finance leadership. Champion volunteer engagement and conversion, building on Bernie's Book Bank's substantial volunteer base and developing stronger pathways from volunteer engagement to long-term advocacy, donor relationships, and philanthropic support. Build a strong and connected team culture, providing clarity, accountability, and support while maintaining the collaborative, flexible, and mission-driven culture that characterizes the Chicago team. Location, Compensation and Benefits This position is based at Bernie's Book Bank's headquarters and Processing Center in Lake Bluff, Illinois, with regular travel throughout Chicagoland for donor meetings, events, board engagements, community activities, and partner visits. The role will include some evening and weekend commitments. A salary range of $160,000 - $175,000 is offered for this role. Additionally, Bernie's Book Bank offers a benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, disability coverage, paid time off, and a 401(k) program. All inquiries and discussions will be handled with the utmost confidentiality. This position is available immediately, and applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until the role is filled. We look forward to receiving your interest.

review_candidates.title: (Associate) Director, Expansion & Partnerships, AI Access Initiative (EAII)
review_candidates.description: This position is with EAII Advisors, Evidence Action's technical partner in India. About EAII EAII Advisors, Evidence Action's technical partner in India, supports state governments in delivering evidence-based public health programs, including safe drinking water initiatives and school and Anganwadi-based National Deworming Day and iron and folic acid supplementation. Operating across 10 states, EAII Advisors provides technical assistance to ministries of health, education, water, and women and child development, reducing health burdens in impoverished communities and improving the long-term wellbeing of children and families. For more information, read about our work here: About Evidence Action and EAII About The AI Access Initiative (2AI) We're at an inflection point in artificial intelligence - presenting both tremendous potential opportunity and risk for people in developing countries. AI capabilities are improving on a timescale measured in months, while development systems often move on timescales measured in decades. Much of the technology needed for positive impact exists today, but few organizations exist to bridge research, deployment, and scaled implementation: we must act now to ensure AI's benefits reach people in poverty in LMICs. Incubated at Evidence Action, we're scaling The AI Access Initiative, an organization focused on scaling AI-enabled 'big bets' to benefit tens or hundreds of millions of people in poverty in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). We operate at the intersection of global development actors, top AI labs, and leading researchers to drive meaningful access to AI's benefits for the 3.5 billion people living in poverty globally. We create "public good," open-sourced playbooks, toolkits, and insights that define how to design and launch tractable and impactful AI-enabled programs. Given the scale of opportunity, we expect our portfolio to expand substantially, but to start, we're scaling two programs focused on AI in Agriculture and AI in Health. We are led by former Evidence Action CEO Kanika Bahl, a founding member of Anthropic's Long-Term Benefit Trust, and advised by Nobel Laureate Michael Kremer; Dario Amodei, CEO of Anthropic; and Kent Walker, President, Global Affairs for Alphabet and Google. This work builds on Evidence Action's track record reaching 530M+ people with cost-effective, evidence-based programs across 9 countries in Africa and Asia, with a focus on last-mile delivery. The Role 2AI is building fast. We have a founding team, two live program portfolios, and a pipeline of opportunities that will drive significant expansion. The programs we are running have credible pathways to 100s of millions of people. While incubated at Evidence Action, we plan to spin out in Q4 '26. Our Agriculture portfolio is scaling AI-enabled weather forecasting services to reach tens of millions of smallholder farmers, in close partnership with state and national governments in India. The next phase is to expand this work: deciding which countries we move into next and building what it takes to operate there. We are seeking a rigorous, high-ownership Associate Director or Director, Expansion & Partnerships to own that expansion end to end, from market selection and government and telco partnerships through to standing up offices and teams in new markets. This role is based in India and sits on 2AI's global team, reporting into the VP, Agriculture. It includes people leadership, managing at least one senior manager across the program. You will work closely with our India country team and other in-country team members to scope and expand programming. You Will: Identify new markets for forecast delivery: In conjunction with the VP, Agriculture, develop the criteria for market selection and prioritize countries to expand into Stand up new markets: Once a new market is confirmed, support the set-up of offices and the hiring of high-quality staff with the requisite skills to implement large-scale forecast delivery Oversee development of forecasts for new regions: Collaborate with academics to ensure forecasts are developed, tested, and ready to disseminate in new countries. This could include hiring and managing post-doctoral students to support in model benchmarking or dataset support Lead telco partnerships: Identify target telcos and lead engagement, negotiation, and relationship management to set up sustainable telco-based dissemination systems Hire and manage in-country scoping support: Where staff on the ground are needed to determine whether there is an opportunity in a new market, hire and oversee them, for example short-term consultants Build and maintain government relationships: Create new and nurture existing relationships with the government bodies needed to operate and disseminate forecasts in a new market, including agriculture departments and meteorological agencies Partner with stakeholders: Create new and nurture existing relationships with academic institutions, delivery partners, and other agriculture organizations. Develop best practices and thought leadership: Across all of the above, build best practices and replicable toolkits that can be applied elsewhere by others. Share key learnings with the sector through toolkits, blogs, and other public-good resources Requirements The ideal candidate is an exceptional builder with the ability to drive outcomes in a fast-moving, high-stakes environment. Given the startup nature of this work, we seek contributors with high throughput, strong work ethic, and willingness to lean in and work extended hours. You will likely have: 7-10+ years' experience as a builder in international development, consulting, or an agriculture adjacent organization Strong communication skills in English with experience working with international teams A proven track record of significantly scaling organizations and/or programs to deliver impact at scale, preferably in close partnership with national governments. Direct experience taking a program or organization into a new region is a plus Demonstrated success building and negotiating partnerships with governments and the private sector. Experience with telcos, mobile network operators, or platform partners is a strong plus Training or early career experience in a high-rigor environment (e.g., top-tier management consulting, high-growth NGO program leadership, strategy/econ research) and the ability to rapidly get up to speed in new technical areas including AI/ML forecasting concepts A track record as a strong people manager and builder: able to set clear standards, empower others, and cultivate a high-performance culture across distributed and field-based teams Experience working with Asian and/or African governments to drive large-scale change, with a strong preference for direct experience working with ministries of agriculture or national meteorological agencies High EQ and the ability to influence across diverse partners, from AI/forecasting researchers to frontline delivery staff to senior government officials Strong fluency with AI tools, and eager to experiment, learn, and adapt to emerging technologies Comfort with ambiguity and fast iteration; can define and test hypotheses, adapt quickly, and maintain focus on impact Excellent written and verbal communication skills; able to synthesize complex technical ideas (e.g., AI/ML weather forecasting language) into crisp narratives for different audiences Willingness and ability to travel extensively internationally (:40-50%) to prospective and current markets across low-and-middle income countries Passion for the mission of ensuring that the benefits of frontier AI reach the world's poorest populations, while mitigating its downside risks Position Location This role is based in India, with flexibility on location within the country. The role sits on 2AI's global team rather than within a single country program, and requires significant international travel (:40-50%) to prospective and current markets. Evidence Action is an Equal Opportunity Employer with a commitment to diversity. All individuals, regardless of personal characteristics, are encouraged to apply. Applicants must be legally authorized to work in India. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of employment visas at this time. Benefits EAII provides a comprehensive benefits package for employees . Benefits include: Comprehensive health insurance with IPD and OPD provisions, Life and Accidental insurance, PF, ESIC and Gratuity as per statutory requirements, Generous leave, Mental and physical wellbeing benefits Learning & Development benefits Avenues for engagement and recognition Compensation: Pay will be competitive and commensurate with the individual's credentials, experience and previous pay scale. This role will initially be housed at EAII Advisors, Evidence Action's technical partner in India, with the explicit plan to transfer with the AI Access Initiative as a founding member of the team when that project is spun out as a new entity later this year. At that point, benefits and policies may change.
